title: Strict henselization under a quasi-finite local map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, let $p\subset A$ and $q\subset B$ be primes with $q$ lying over $p$, and assume $A\to B$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (in particular this applies when $A\to B$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]). Choose an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and compatible geometric point maps $\kappa(p)\to\Omega$ and $\kappa(q)\to\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the strict henselizations formed from the pointed etale-neighbourhood colimits with the induced separable closures in $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Then the canonical map $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}\to B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a finite local homomorphism. Its residue-field extension is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Moreover $B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is canonically the localization of $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A_p}B_q$ at the prime ideal which is the kernel of the induced map $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A_p}B_q\to\Omega$.

proof.text: Put $R=A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $H=B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $K=\kappa(R)$ and $L=\kappa(H)$. Apply strict-henselization functoriality to $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the specified compatible geometric points. Its clauses (1)--(3) give strictly henselian local rings $R,H$, embeddings $K\subset L\subset\Omega$, and the canonical local map $h:R\to H$ over $A\to B$ inducing this inclusion. These are the pointed-neighbourhood colimits in the statement. Set $C=R\otimes_A B$ and let $\epsilon:C\to\Omega$ send $r\otimes b$ to the product of their given images in $\Omega$. The prime $\mathfrak n=\ker\epsilon$ contracts to $\mathfrak m_R$ in $R$ and to $q$ in $B$: the respective maps to $\Omega$ factor through the injectively embedded residue fields. Set $D=C_{\mathfrak n}$.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), and the functoriality paragraph following Tag 03PS; algebra.tex Tag 05WR, setup

proof.text: Apply the four-rings lemma with the original rings $A,B$ and their base changes $R,C$. The canonical map $B\otimes_A R\to C$ is the tensor symmetry isomorphism, hence surjective; $A\to B$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the contraction $q$ of $\mathfrak n$. Consequently $R\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $\mathfrak n$, which lies over the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$.

source.place: Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings), as used in the second paragraph of the proof of Tag 05WR

proof.text: Apply the henselian finite-type product decomposition to $R\to C$, obtaining $C\cong A_1\times\cdots\times A_s\times C_0$ with each $A_i$ local finite over $R$ and $C_0$ not quasi-finite over $R$ at any prime over $\mathfrak m_R$. A prime of a finite product selects exactly one factor: modulo a prime the orthogonal idempotents have values $0$ or $1$, and exactly one is $1$. If $\mathfrak n$ selected $C_0$, the four-rings lemma applied to the quotient $C\to C_0$ would make that prime quasi-finite over $R$, a contradiction. Thus it selects $A_i$. The corresponding prime of $A_i$ is maximal: its quotient is a finite-dimensional domain over $K$, hence a field, since multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and therefore surjective on that finite-dimensional vector space. As $A_i$ is local, this prime is its maximal ideal and $D=C_{\mathfrak n}\cong A_i$. In particular $D$ is finite over $R$, is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak nD$, and $R\to D$ is local by the contraction computed in Step 1. The finite-local henselian lemma makes $D$ henselian.

source.place: Tag 04GJ (lemma-mop-up) and Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian), (2)--(3); reconstructing (3) from the existing decomposition nodes

proof.text: Let $E=D/\mathfrak nD$. Because $R\to D$ is local and module finite, any finite set of $R$-module generators of $D$ maps to a spanning set of the $K$-vector space $E$: $\mathfrak m_RD$ acts trivially in this quotient. Thus $E/K$ is a finite field extension. The finite-extension lemma for a separably closed field gives that $E$ is separably closed. For pure inseparability apply the separable-first lemma to $E/K$. Its separable intermediate field is $K$: every separable element generates a finite separable extension of $K$, which is trivial by the definition of separably closed. Hence $E/K$ is purely inseparable, and it is finite as already shown. Since $D$ is henselian and its residue field $E$ is separably closed, $D$ is strictly henselian.

source.place: Tag 030K (lemma-separable-first); algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian) and 05WR, finite purely inseparable residue-field argument

proof.text: The affine-chart ind-etale theorem applied to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B$ gives that $A\to R$ and $B\to H$ are ind-etale. By base-change stability $B\to C=R\otimes_A B$ is ind-etale. The localization $C\to D$ is ind-etale as well: $C_{\mathfrak n}=\varinjlim_{f\notin\mathfrak n}C_f$, with the system directed by taking products of denominators. A fraction $c/f$ is represented in $C_f$, and an equality of two fractions holds after further inverting one element outside $\mathfrak n$, which verifies the colimit description. Each $C\to C_f$ is etale of finite presentation by the principal-localization clause applied to the identity etale $C$-algebra. Thus it is ind-etale by definition. Composition stability now makes $B\to D$ ind-etale. We have exhibited $D$ and $H$ as ind-etale algebras over the same ring $B$.

source.place: Base-change and composition assertions; algebra.tex Tag 00U2 (lemma-etale), (1); Tag 05WR, localization as a filtered colimit of etale algebras

proof.text: The maps $h:R\to H$ and $B\to H$ give a ring map $g:C\to H$ by $g(r\otimes b)=h(r)b$. Its composite with the residue embedding $H\to L\hookrightarrow\Omega$ is $\epsilon$, so $g^{-1}(\mathfrak m_H)=\mathfrak n$. Every $f\notin\mathfrak n$ therefore maps to a unit of the local ring $H$, giving a unique $B$-algebra map $\widetilde g:D=C_{\mathfrak n}\to H$ with $\widetilde g(c/f)=g(c)g(f)^{-1}$. Its inverse image of $\mathfrak m_H$ is exactly $\mathfrak nD$, so it is local. Since $D$ and $H$ are ind-etale over $B$, the relative assertion of ind-etale stability makes this $B$-algebra map ind-etale, hence weakly etale. Apply the weakly-etale strict-local theorem to $\widetilde g$: its source $D$ is strictly henselian by Step 4 and both rings are local, so $\widetilde g$ is an isomorphism. Its composite with $R\to D$ is precisely the original $h$, by its tensor formula.

source.place: Tag 092Z (theorem-olivier); the relative assertion of ind-etale stability realizes the uniqueness step in algebra.tex Tag 05WR

proof.text: Every element of $A\setminus p$ is already a unit in $R$, and every $b\in B\setminus q$ has nonzero image in $\Omega$, so its image in $C$ lies outside $\mathfrak n$. The localization universal property therefore identifies $C_{\mathfrak n}$ canonically with the localization of $R\otimes_{A_p}B_q$ at the kernel of its induced map to $\Omega$: in both rings exactly the elements outside that kernel are inverted. The isomorphism of Step 6 identifies this ring with $H$ via its structural maps. It carries the finite local map $R\to D$ to $h:R\to H$ and the finite purely inseparable extension $E/K$ to its residue extension. This proves every clause. In the parenthetical finite case, the finite-ring-map lemma supplies both finite type and quasi-finiteness at $q$, so the same proof applies.

The explicit finite-type hypothesis is part of the quasi-finite definition, as in Stacks. Nothing is weakened. Step 1: the map epsilon is well defined because functoriality (1) gives the kappa(p)-algebra identification and the geometric points are compatible; n contracts to m_R and to q. Step 2: the 00PN four-rings hypotheses hold because the tensor map is an isomorphism. Step 3: 04GJ applies; the four-rings lemma applied to the quotient onto the residual factor C_0 rules that factor out; the chosen prime is maximal by the finite-domain argument; 04GH(2) then makes D henselian. Step 4: E is separably closed by the finite-extension lemma, and purely inseparable over K by 030K with separable part equal to K, including characteristic 0. Step 5: the affine-chart lemma applies with the identity chart; base change, localization as a colimit of the C_f, and composition are all valid. Step 6: g is well defined by functoriality (3); g inverse of m_H equals n; the map D to H is a local B-algebra map; the relative ind-etale clause makes it weakly etale; the 092Z node's hypotheses hold exactly, so it is an isomorphism compatible with h. This valid agent route replaces the 08HV-plus-uniqueness ending of 05WR and is declared by=agent. Step 7: the localization identification is elementary, and the finite case follows from 00PM. Edge cases checked: B=A_f, a purely inseparable field extension over an imperfect field, a split etale double cover, and nonreduced fibres or several local factors. All cited units lie on the route of sk-i-curve-zero, so the six declared tool_uses are harmless; I accept them.
